anansi.scope: Akan trickster traditions and their African-diaspora continuities; not a single universal spider figure.

sources.title: Ashanti Folk Tales from Ghana
sources.publisher: Smithsonian Center for Folklife and Cultural Heritage

sources.title: Storytelling in the African Diaspora
sources.publisher: National Museum of African American History and Culture

ares.scope: Greek Ares in archaic and classical literary sources; Roman Mars treated as a distinct later religious context.

sources.title: Ares: God of War and Battlelust

asclepius.scope: Greek healing cult, especially Epidaurus; inscriptional testimonies are presented as religious evidence, not clinical proof.

sources.title: The Sanctuary of Asclepius at Epidaurus in Roman Times
Notes on the Epidaurian Building Inscriptions

ame-no-uzume.scope: Ame-no-Uzume in the Kojiki and Nihon shoki; later ritual and lineage associations are kept distinct.

sources.title: The Sun Goddess Amaterasu and the Cave of Heaven

anahita-ar-dvi-sura-anahita.scope: Arədvī Sūrā Anāhitā in Avestan and later Iranian contexts; no assumption of an unchanged continuous identity.

ark-of-the-covenant.scope: Ark as represented in biblical texts and later interpretation; no claim that a physical object survives or has been located.

baba-yaga.scope: East Slavic folktale variants; no claim that one version exhausts Russian, Ukrainian, or Belarusian traditions.

sources.title: Baba Yaga
sources.publisher: University of Southern California Digital Folklore Archives

sources.title: Baba Yaga: The Wild Witch of the East in Russian Fairy Tales
sources.publisher: University Press of Mississippi via UBC Press

medusa.scope: Medusa in ancient Greek literary and visual traditions; later retellings are not treated as the only classical account.

sources.title: Dangerous Beauty: Medusa in Classical Art

persephone.scope: Persephone in the Homeric Hymn to Demeter and later Greek and Roman retellings; the hymn is not treated as a complete universal account.

gilgamesh.scope: The Babylonian Epic of Gilgamesh as a surviving, multi-tablet textual tradition; gaps and variants remain visible.

sources.title: Epic of Gilgamesh, Old Babylonian Version

mami-wata.scope: Mami Wata traditions in Africa and the African Atlantic world; no reduction of distinct water-spirit traditions to one origin or figure.

sources.title: Mami Wata: Arts for Water Spirits in Africa and Its Diasporas

quetzalcoatl.scope: Feathered-serpent imagery across Mesoamerica and Quetzalcoatl in central Mexican contexts; cultural and chronological differences are retained.

sources.title: Serpent mask of Quetzalcoatl or Tlaloc
The Temple of Quetzalcoatl at Teotihuacan
